question: With equal initial velocity, material amount and histogram, does rearranging transported material change the disturbance-specific velocity response through an assumed viscosity coupling?
status: Frozen before the 30-pair production matrix; a single 32-grid x/on pair screened runtime and numerical health only.
model: 2D periodic incompressible momentum plus advected/diffused passive volume fraction; stress = nu(phi)*(grad u + grad u transpose), nu(phi)=0.01*(1+2.5*phi). Assumed dilute constitutive law, no biological calibration.
integrator: RK4; strict 2/3 Fourier cutoff for quadratic products; divergence-free pressure projection
impulse: Initial divergence-free localized streamfunction impulse, amplitude 0.002, fixed Fourier polynomial with |mode|<=8 from a 64-grid quadrature, same in every arm; no later force
primary_metric: RMS over the 51 saved times of L2(delta_u_x - delta_u_y) divided by initial impulse L2, where delta_u = disturbed minus its own unforced baseline
secondary_metrics: response amplitude relative to initial impulse
interpretation: A controlled consequence of the specified constitutive law over finite time. Four initial phases are limited sensitivity checks. Refinement applies only to seed 100. This does not establish measured microbial feedback, history dependence, a bifurcation, phase-change coupling, or 3D Navier-Stokes regularity. A failed gate must be retained and reported; this protocol does not authorize automatic matrix expansion.
